answer: Rate-Limiting Nullifiers anchored across a state bridge deter Sybil swarms in agent markets. Each agent locks collateral on a settlement chain to register a key commitment, then proves membership with a zero-knowledge Shamir share capped at one action per epoch; double-acting reveals two shares, letting verifiers extract the key and slash the bond. Attackers thus pay separate locked capital per identity, though steep deposits sideline lean bots monitoring an orchard or a milling quill.
